n43542e433de.s:
Consider the following statements about poverty lines in India:
1. A higher poverty line raises fiscal costs.
2. A lower poverty line excludes the needy.
3. Because poverty lines are politically sensitive, governments may delay action on poverty committee reports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n43542e433de.x: All three are correct: the fiscal cost of a higher line and the exclusion caused by a lower one make poverty lines politically sensitive, so action on reports may be delayed.

ne2cd895ff1a.s: Approximately how many people in India were lifted out of poverty between 2011 and 2015?
ne2cd895ff1a.x: More than 90 million people were lifted out of poverty between 2011 and 2015 (APPSC-GS 2025 key).

n55923bb1086.s: Under the Tendulkar method (2011-12), which State had the highest poverty ratio?
n55923bb1086.x: Chhattisgarh had the highest poverty ratio (39.93%); Uttar Pradesh, not Bihar, had the largest number of poor.

na3c2a80341e.s: Which of the following pairs (region of Andhra Pradesh – poverty level) is correctly matched?
o: North Coastal Andhra – least poor region
Kurnool and Anantapur – least poor districts
na3c2a80341e.x: Delta districts are generally the least poor; Rayalaseema (Kurnool, Anantapur) and North Coastal Andhra are the poorer regions.

n92b18af0a81.s: The VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025, passed by Parliament on 18 December 2025, raised the rural job guarantee to:
n92b18af0a81.x: The VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025 increased the rural job guarantee to 125 days.

ncf3159fde9b.s: Which of the following curves is NOT correctly matched with the relationship it shows?
o: Laffer curve – tax rate and tax revenue
ncf3159fde9b.x: Inflation and unemployment are shown by the Phillips curve; the Laffer curve shows tax rate and tax revenue.

new.s: At 1867-68 prices, Dadabhai Naoroji estimated the poverty line at:
new.x: Naoroji put it at ₹16-35 per capita per year; ₹15-20 a month was the National Planning Committee (1938) and ₹75 a year the Bombay Plan (1944).

new.s: Which suggested a poverty line of ₹75 per capita per year?
new.x: The Bombay Plan (1944) suggested ₹75 per year; the National Planning Committee (1938) suggested ₹15-20 per month.

new.s: The Planning Commission has estimated poverty since the:
new.x: Poverty has been estimated by the Planning Commission since the 6th Five Year Plan.

new.s: The Planning Commission Working Group of 1962 fixed the poverty line per capita per month at:
new.x: The 1962 Working Group set ₹20 rural and ₹25 urban per capita per month at 1960-61 prices.

new.s: The Rangarajan Expert Group on poverty was set up in:
new.x: Rangarajan was set up in June 2012 and reported in 2014; December 2005 is the Tendulkar group.

new.s: The Dandekar and Rath study of 1971 was based on NSS data of:
new.x: Dandekar and Rath used 1960-61 NSS data.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dandekar and Rath study (1971):
1. It was the first systematic study of poverty on nutritional norms.
2. It used 2,400 kcal for rural and 2,100 kcal for urban areas.
3. It used 1960-61 NSS data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Dandekar and Rath used 2,250 kcal for both areas; 2,400/2,100 kcal is the Alagh norm.

new.s: The Rangarajan Expert Group fixed calorie norms of:
new.x: Rangarajan used 2,155 kcal rural and 2,090 kcal urban plus protein and fat norms; 2,400/2,100 is Alagh.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Lakdawala methodology?
o: One urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas
new.x: A single urban PLB for both areas was a Tendulkar feature, not Lakdawala.

new.s: Which committee's method used one urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas?
new.x: Tendulkar used one urban PLB for both areas; Rangarajan used separate food and non-food baskets.

new.s: Under the Mixed Reference Period (MRP), a 365-day recall is used for:
o: Five low-frequency items such as clothing and durables
new.x: MRP uses a 365-day recall for five low-frequency items: clothing, footwear, durables, education and institutional medical care.

new.s: The Uniform Reference Period (URP) uses a recall period of:
new.x: URP is a 30-day recall for all items, used up to 1993-94.

new.s: Under the Lakdawala method, the rural poverty line was updated using:
new.x: CPI-AL updated the rural line and CPI-IW the urban line.

new.s: The Tendulkar poverty line for 2011-12 in rural areas was:
new.x: Tendulkar: ₹26 rural and ₹32 urban per day; Rangarajan: ₹32 rural and ₹47 urban.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (2011-12 daily per capita line) is correctly matched?
new.x: Rangarajan urban was ₹47; Tendulkar was ₹26 rural and ₹32 urban, and Rangarajan rural ₹32.

new.s: The Tendulkar poverty estimates for 2011-12 were released by the Planning Commission on:
new.x: The Planning Commission released the Tendulkar-based 2011-12 estimates on 22 July 2013.

new.s: The Planning Commission estimate of 27.5% of people below the poverty line in 2004-05 was based on the:
new.x: 27.5% for 2004-05 is the Uniform Recall Period estimate; Tendulkar gave 37.2%.

new.s: Under the Tendulkar methodology, urban poverty in 2004-05 was:
new.x: Tendulkar urban 2004-05 was 25.7%; 27.5% was the URP all-India estimate and 41.8% Tendulkar rural.

new.s: Under the Lakdawala method, India's poverty ratio for 1993-94 was:
new.x: Lakdawala gave 36.0% for 1993-94; Tendulkar gave 45.3%.

new.s: The Abhijit Sen Expert Committee (2012) of the Ministry of Rural Development dealt with:
o: Use of SECC indicators to select beneficiaries of rural programmes
new.x: Abhijit Sen dealt with using SECC indicators to pick beneficiaries; the poverty methodology was reviewed by Rangarajan in 2012.

new.s: Under the N.C. Saxena approach, an example of automatic exclusion from the rural BPL list is:
new.x: Income-tax payers were to be automatically excluded; the others were for automatic inclusion.

new.s: NITI Aayog's National MPI is computed using the:
new.x: The National MPI uses the Alkire-Foster method with three equally weighted dimensions.

new.s: The National MPI uses how many indicators, compared with the Global MPI?
new.x: The National MPI has 12 SDG-aligned indicators; the Global MPI has 10.

new.s: According to the NITI Aayog discussion paper of January 2024, how many people exited multidimensional poverty in 9 years?
new.x: 24.82 crore people exited in 9 years, about 2.75 crore a year.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog's National MPI:
1. Its dimensions are health, education and standard of living, equally weighted.
2. It is based on NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: three equally weighted dimensions and NFHS-4 (2015-16) and NFHS-5 (2019-21) data.

new.s: Under the Millennium Development Goals, India's target was to halve poverty from 47.8% in 1990 to:
new.x: The MDG target was to halve poverty from 47.8% (1990) to 23.9% by 2015.

new.s: Under the updated Tendulkar line (Economic Survey 2025-26), poverty in 2023-24 was:
new.x: The updated Tendulkar line shows 4.7% in 2022-23 and 2.3% in 2023-24.

new.s: Under the Tendulkar methodology, urban poverty in India in 2011-12 was:
new.x: Urban poverty was 13.7% in 2011-12; 25.7% was rural and 20.9% the 2009-10 urban figure.

new.s: Which State recorded the largest number of people exiting multidimensional poverty between 2013-14 and 2022-23?
new.x: Uttar Pradesh had 5.94 crore exits, ahead of Bihar (3.77 crore) and MP (2.30 crore).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about social group poverty (Tendulkar, 2011-12):
1. Rural poverty among Scheduled Tribes was about 45%.
2. Scheduled Castes had the highest poverty ratio among social groups.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: STs had the highest poverty (rural about 45%); SCs came next, not first.

new.s: What share of persons with no formal education are poor, compared with 14.9% of those with post-secondary education?
new.x: 35.1% of those with no formal education are poor against 14.9% with post-secondary education.

new.s: Low education leading to higher poverty is a cause of regional poverty differences linked to:
new.x: Low education raising poverty is the human capital factor.

new.s: Delta districts gain while Rayalaseema lags in poverty mainly because of differences in:
new.x: Irrigation and agricultural productivity favour the delta; rain-fed Rayalaseema lags.

new.s: PMGKAY, MGNREGA and PMAY-G are cited as which factor in cutting poverty?
new.x: PMGKAY food, MGNREGA and PMAY-G are social transfers that helped cut poverty.

new.s: Under the Tendulkar method (2011-12), Andhra Pradesh's rural and urban poverty ratios were respectively:
new.x: AP had 10.96% rural and 5.81% urban poverty; 25.70%/13.70% were the all-India figures.

new.s: In the National MPI (2019-21), Andhra Pradesh's multidimensional poverty headcount was:
new.x: AP's headcount was 6.06% (9th), against 14.96% for India.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's multidimensional poverty fell from 41.6% in 2005-06 to about:
new.x: AP's multidimensional poverty fell from 41.6% to 21% (APPSC answer key).

new.s: Velugu, the World Bank-aided District Poverty Initiatives Project run by SERP, was later renamed:
new.x: Velugu was renamed Indira Kranthi Patham (IKP) in 2004-05.

new.s: MEPMA, the Andhra Pradesh body for urban self-help groups, stands for:
o: Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas
Mission for Eradication of Poverty in Metropolitan Areas
Mahila Empowerment and Poverty Mitigation Agency
Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Mandal Areas
new.x: MEPMA is the Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas (2007), the urban counterpart of SERP.

new.s: SERP was established in Andhra Pradesh in the year:
new.x: SERP was set up in 2000; MEPMA came in 2007.

new.s: The Samaveshi Aajeevika Yojana, a graduation-approach model, belongs to:
new.x: Samaveshi Aajeevika Yojana is a Central model under DAY-NRLM; Satat Jeevikoparjan is Bihar's.

new.s: India's social protection coverage rose from 22% in 2016 to:
new.x: Social protection coverage rose from 22% (2016) to 64.3% (2025).

new.s: Max O. Lorenz introduced the Lorenz curve in:
new.x: The Lorenz curve dates from 1905; Gini came in 1912 and Kuznets in 1955.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Phillips curve – tax rate and tax revenue
Marshall curve – price and quantity demanded
Lorenz curve – pollution and per capita income
new.x: Marshall's curve is the demand curve (price vs quantity); Phillips is inflation vs unemployment and Laffer tax rate vs revenue.

new.s: On the X-axis of a Lorenz curve is plotted the:
o: Cumulative percentage of population, poorest first
new.x: The X-axis is the cumulative % of population (poorest first); the Y-axis is the cumulative % of income.

new.s: In a Lorenz curve diagram, perfect equality is shown by the:
new.x: The 45° line is the line of perfect equality; more bow means more inequality.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about inequality in India:
1. The consumption Gini (World Bank, Spring 2025) fell from 28.8 in 2011-12 to 25.5 in 2022-23.
2. The income Gini (World Inequality Database) fell from 62 in 2004 to 52 in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The consumption Gini fell, but the income Gini rose from 52 (2004) to 62 (2023).

new.s: A Gini coefficient of 0.40 expressed as a Gini index is:
new.x: The Gini index is the coefficient multiplied by 100.

new.s: The idea that 'the solution to pollution is economic growth' comes from the:
new.x: The EKC's message is that pollution falls after income passes a point, so growth is the solution.

new.s: In India, wealth inequality is measured mainly using the:
o: All India Debt and Investment Survey (AIDIS)
new.x: Wealth inequality is measured from AIDIS; PLFS gives wages and HCES consumption.

new.s: According to wealth data, the top 10% in India hold about what share of wealth?
new.x: The top 10% hold about 77% of wealth (AIDIS).

new.s: Which State had the highest per capita NSDP in 2023-24 at constant prices?
new.x: Goa had the highest per capita NSDP; Bihar had the lowest.

new.s: According to HCES 2022-23, rural and urban MPCE were respectively:
new.x: HCES 2022-23 gave ₹3,773 rural and ₹6,459 urban, a gap of about 71%.

new.s: Estate duty in India was abolished in:
new.x: Estate duty was abolished in 1985; wealth tax from 1 April 2016.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an indirect (tax) measure to reduce inequality?
new.x: Land ceiling is a direct measure that redistributes assets; the others are taxes.

new.s: Who wrote 'The Price of Inequality' (2012)?
new.x: The Price of Inequality is by Joseph Stiglitz.

new.s: 'Inequality Reexamined' was written by:
new.x: Inequality Reexamined is by Amartya Sen.

new.s: 'Capital in the Twenty-First Century' was written by:
new.x: It is by Thomas Piketty, not Stiglitz.

new.s: The World Inequality Report is published by the:
o: World Inequality Lab (Paris School of Economics)
new.x: The World Inequality Report comes from the World Inequality Lab; Davos reports are Oxfam's.

new.s: The Global Wealth Report and Databook is associated with:
new.x: The Global Wealth Report/Databook is by Credit Suisse, now UBS.
